fatal_errors: The proposed sluggish-diffusion, entropy-stabilization mechanism is opposite to the observed active diffusion and kinetically controlled surface segregation.
It predicts retention of chemical uniformity, whereas the target evidence shows Au/Cu surface segregation, melting or evaporation, particle loss, and approximately 22% size reduction.

The composition-perturbation intervention does not isolate configurational entropy because it simultaneously changes surface energies, mixing thermodynamics, melting behavior, and elemental volatility.
No supporting or conflicting evidence is cited.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses thermal stability of near-equiatomic multielement nanoparticles and offers a nominally testable comparison, but it largely restates the conventional high-entropy/sluggish-diffusion baseline that the target study disproves. It does not reconstruct the AuCoCuNiPt sub-10 nm FCC multi-twinned system, vacuum heating to 973 K, stepped in situ STEM-EDS measurements, or atomistic simulations. The target mechanism is size- and shape-dependent active diffusion driven by surface-energy minimization, with Au and Cu enriching the surface and ultimately melting or evaporating above roughly 673 K. The proposed experiment could test whether composition correlates with stability, but it cannot uniquely attribute any difference to configurational entropy. A discriminating design would instead track temperature-dependent Au self-diffusivity, surface Au/Cu enrichment, shape evolution, and mass or size loss against the sluggish-diffusion prediction under identical vacuum heating.
